item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I've always felt that Gears really shines with prose, particularly short stories. I can't think of another writer here that approaches his skill with tales.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Oddly enough…..I'd call this Lovecraftian style writing. Modern setting, modern way of putting things, but Lovecraft in the fear of the unknown and mind-numbing horror that you try your best to simply forget. The insinuation of it following him home fits in too. Spectacularly written, love it as always.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The throwaway 'rape' line early on was really distracting, for like ten different reasons (but ultimately, it being really distracting was most relevant).

Besides that, I loved this. That dog-man is… fucking intense. And calling it a 'dog-man' does a good job of underpreparing you for the reality of the thing.

item.title: If the dog man bites, do I get shots?
item.content:encoded: Am I the only one worried about Mrs. Gears and the kid falling asleep while driving?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: My wife swears she fell asleep at the wheel and saw something that totally wasn't real, and made the mistake of telling me about it. Also, the Michigan Dog Man is a thing, and this is sort of the blending of the two. Also, a dog-man is also a term for cowardly folk, so double irony there.
